tool_input.prompt:
Create ONLY a hand-drawn 2D game character.
STYLE C: a hand-drawn 2D painted sprite combining Hollow Knight's compact rounded shapes with Diablo II's worn dark mood. Use broad dry-brush patches, subtle mottled pigment and angular flat shadow cutouts, thin broken colored edges and economical ring-mail marks. This must look like a tiny weathered painted game actor, darker and rougher than a clean animation cel, simpler than a detailed fantasy illustration. No smooth gradient modeling, heavy ink contours or decorative comic hatching.

MANDATORY: ONLY TWO-DIMENSIONAL (2D) ART. No three-dimensional (3D) render, sculpt, model, miniature photograph, plastic or clay figure, realistic material shader, glossy metal or studio lighting. Draw by hand as a 2D game asset; use painted marks and flat shadow shapes to describe the elevated view. Create one original full-body character on a square canvas, plain charcoal-black background and small simple painted floor shadow. No writing, captions or panels.

APPROVED MOOD-BOARD CONTEXT: Hollow Knight is the strongest guide for large-head/tiny-body structure, simple shapes, restrained contours and luminous darkness (approved M22–M25). Diablo II guides dark earthen colors, worn materials and elevated gameplay composition (M20–M21); its realistic anatomy and 3D material rendering must not transfer. Castle Crashers contributes only a trace of short squat proportions, never its bright colors or comedy (M26). Darkwood contributes quiet unease and darkness, not its camera (M19). The sacred paintings M01–M03 contribute soot-black recesses, muted bone/iron whites and dried blood red, not their later costume or spectacle. Overall feeling: solemn, weather-beaten, lonely, faintly uncanny, with an endearing compact silhouette. Neither cheerful comic-book illustration nor polished heroic fantasy.

SUBJECT AND PROPORTIONS: Guarin, a road-worn household knight returning to the Royans/Isere lands in 1101. An ENORMOUS barrel helmet on a TINY BROAD BODY with very short stubby arms and legs and small wide boots. Approximately two helmet-heights tall in unprojected proportions, head wider than torso. Cute and squat, no anatomically realistic adult warrior. His face and eyes are entirely concealed. Neutral quiet idle stance facing diagonally lower-right, all equipment and feet visible.

CAMERA: very elevated orthographic three-quarter gameplay view, looking steeply DOWN from 60 degrees above the ground. Helmet remains upright, its flat circular lid LEVEL, not tilted toward the viewer. Show a broad deep lid ellipse and compress the short front plate, shoulders almost hidden beneath the huge lid, belly and stubby legs strongly foreshortened. Keep the high view coherent across helmet, shield rim and boot tops. Render this projection with 2D drawn planes, not a 3D object.

FIXED COSTUME: plain dull-iron fully enclosed cylindrical GREATHELM, flat unadorned crown, two plain vertical riveted strips, one narrow black visor slit and small round breathing holes. Fine interlocking RING MAIL shirt and short sleeves, drawn as tiny joined C/O curves, not overlapping scales, isolated polka dots or huge metal disks. Ragged faded dark wine-red scarf and short cape, matching ragged waist cloth. Brown leather belt with one plain rectangular buckle, plain brown gloves, taupe/brown forearm and shin wraps, short round brown boots. Straight double-edged arming sword in viewer-left hand: disk pommel, brown grip, straight crossguard and rigid straight symmetric blade pointing down across the front to lower-right. Elongated taupe wooden KITE SHIELD at viewer-right, dull iron rim, one narrow faded wine-red panel. No extra armor, clothing, insignia, crest, jewelry or weapons. These plain local materials fit the rural Royans/Isere story; the greathelm is the explicitly allowed anachronism, not evidence of 1101 regional use.

COLOR AND READABILITY: weathered warm-dark-gray iron, soot-black shadows, muddy taupe/brown leather and muted dried-wine cloth. Sparse chalk-gray edge marks, matte rough surfaces, no pale shiny silver or bright primary colors. Small controlled areas of light, large quiet areas of dark. Keep the silhouette readable at gameplay size with finely stepped drawn edges rather than large blocky mosaic pixels. Preserve costume and proportions; only the 2D drawing language varies.
